findings: Retain the dated April body and the November index reference. Add the payment-attempt boundary and a verified failure/recovery route, including the `requires_action` decline and HTTP 402 (source 13–34, old raw 211–233 and 327–331). Preserve the existing written-consent and optional CVC/Radar warnings (source 36–76).

Source line 21 presents database persistence as a numbered requirement. The April iOS, Android and React Native bodies instead describe an internal mapping if the merchant has one, and permit storing both IDs or listing saved PaymentMethods using the known customer identity when ready to charge (old raw lines 179-209, 491-521 and 807-837). Keep Accounts v2 `customer_account` confined to the paired guide's listing examples. Its direct-attachment and later-charge examples use Customers v1 `customer` (old raw lines 150-227).

The combined example at source lines 24-34 is a charge-and-save attempt for an existing Customer. The April example sets `confirm: true`, `error_on_requires_action: true` and `setup_future_usage: 'on_session'` (old raw lines 235-254). For this card path the separate November Create PaymentIntent reference (`raw/stripe-api-payment-intents-create-2026-11-07.md:432-444,672-685`) and migration guide (`raw/stripe-payments-payment-intents-migration-2026-11-07.md:131-133`) condition attachment under `setup_future_usage` on successful confirmation and completion of any required customer actions. A failed confirmation is insufficient to mark the method newly saved. The earlier direct-attachment path separately associates the method ahead of the later charge.
conflicts: The dated April guide describes a simpler option for merchants that primarily do business in the US and Canada, and rejects it in countries requiring authentication to save cards, with India as an example (old raw 12–25, 337–350, 631–644). The mapped source line 13 and reciprocal routes in the Stripe index line 128 and concepts `stripe-inapp-payments.md:114` and `stripe-saved-payment-methods.md:157` broaden this to an exclusive US/Canada product eligibility claim. Preserve the April positioning and authentication/compliance conditions as dated, without carrying forward an all-card guarantee within the US or Canada or a fresh legal conclusion.

Mapped source lines 13 and 22–34 connect later charging with a historical `setup_future_usage: 'on_session'` charge-and-save example. Keep that example gated on an existing Customer and scope it to intended future use with the customer present (old raw 235–254). The separate November PaymentIntent Create reference (`raw/stripe-api-payment-intents-create-2026-11-07.md:635-639,672-685`) distinguishes `on_session` and `off_session` future-use values from the attempted charge's `off_session` flag. The November migration guide gives the same on/off distinction for planned future charges (`raw/stripe-payments-payment-intents-migration-2026-11-07.md:127-139`). Add reciprocal scope with the in-app concept's charge-and-save section (42–54) and the saved payment methods concept's off-session guidance (111–121); the April example does not establish suitability for unattended reuse.

The November Attach PaymentMethod API reference (`raw/stripe-api-payment-methods-attach-2026-11-07.md:5-11`) recommends a SetupIntent or PaymentIntent with `setup_future_usage` for future payments, and warns direct attachment alone does not optimize the method for future use. Preserve the dated April direct-attach path (old raw 150–183), but distinguish storage/association from optimized setup and eventual payment. The separate November Create PaymentIntent reference (`raw/stripe-api-payment-intents-create-2026-11-07.md:432-450`) also says this `error_on_requires_action` flag needs `confirm=true` and fails the attempt if the intent transitions to `requires_action`.

contributions.original_prompts:
New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-mobile-save-card-without-authentication-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-inapp-save-card-without-auth-2025.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-inapp-save-card-without-auth.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/save-card-without-authentication`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: The November capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/save-card-without-authentication establishes the purpose of collecting card details in a mobile app for later charging and routes iOS, Android and React Native (new raw lines 5-15). The April 23, 2026 guide presents the simpler route for businesses primarily in the US and Canada, calls for opt-in and written agreement for future use, and warns that it is unsuitable where saving cards requires authentication, such as India (old raw lines 12-25). The dated setup calls for a mobile Stripe SDK configured with the publishable key and merchant-server endpoints that call Stripe's API (old raw lines 27-47, old raw lines 97-116 and old raw lines 646-685). The client creates a PaymentMethod and sends its ID. The server associates it with a new or existing Customer, then separately creates and confirms a PaymentIntent using the saved method. For the later charge the merchant can persist both IDs or list saved PaymentMethods by known customer identity, so persisting the PaymentMethod ID in its own database is optional. The dated listing examples distinguish Customers v1 `customer` from Accounts v2 `customer_account`. The attachment and charge examples use Customers v1 `customer` (old raw lines 118-227, old raw lines 491-521 and old raw lines 807-837). `error_on_requires_action: true` with `confirm: true` fails the payment attempt if customer action is required. The April guide describes HTTP 402, inspecting the decline, and customer recovery or upgrading the integration (old raw lines 211-233 and old raw lines 327-331). source-stripe-inapp-save-card-without-auth.md captures key steps, combined charge-and-save and optional CVC collection, but states a narrower country rule, presents database persistence as a mandatory step, and leaves out the authentication failure boundary.
reviewed_answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/save-card-without-authentication, the November capture moves the same three platform variants to a navigation index (new raw lines 9-15) without documenting fresh behavior or deprecation. source-stripe-inapp-save-card-without-auth.md and its reciprocal concept and index routes should date the April guide's regional positioning, eligibility conditions and consent, decline, UI and SDK details (old raw lines 12-54, old raw lines 211-264 and old raw lines 369-396). Retain the April combined charge-and-save attempt for an existing Customer, which sets `confirm: true`, `error_on_requires_action: true` and `setup_future_usage: 'on_session'` (old raw lines 235-254). For this card path Stripe attaches the PaymentMethod under `setup_future_usage` after successful confirmation and completion of any required customer actions. A failed confirmation does not establish that the method was newly saved. The April examples separately show direct attachment to a Customer before attempting a later charge (old raw lines 150-227; `raw/stripe-api-payment-intents-create-2026-11-07.md:432-444,672-685` and `raw/stripe-payments-payment-intents-migration-2026-11-07.md:131-133`). The separate November Create PaymentIntent capture scopes `on_session` to future reuse with the customer present and distinguishes intended future use from the current charge's `off_session` flag (`raw/stripe-api-payment-intents-create-2026-11-07.md:635-639,672-685`). The November Attach PaymentMethod reference explains that attachment alone lacks future-use optimization and recommends SetupIntent or PaymentIntent with `setup_future_usage` (`raw/stripe-api-payment-methods-attach-2026-11-07.md:5-11`). Preserve those boundaries in the in-app and saved payment methods concept routes so the old example is not taken as authority for unattended or optimized future charging. CVC re-collection uses a separate client confirmation path, and successful payment can coexist with a failed CVC check unless appropriate Radar blocking is configured (old raw lines 266-331 and old raw lines 894-929). The captures document these conditions and examples without proving a successful actual charge, account eligibility or compliance.
